a class of estimators proposed by Hall and Sheather [1988] are uniformly, strongly convergent when the bandwidth is allowed to be a random variable.

the proposed estimators have the following properties: (a) the estimators are consistent; (b) the estimators do not require knowledge of the noise distribution; (c) the estimators can be applied to any distribution; (d) the estimators use only one kernel function and one bandwidth; and (e) the estimators require less computation than the previously proposed estimations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed class of estimators can be used in practice without the need to choose the constants.
the proposed estimator can be made to perform well even when the constants are chosen in an ad hoc fashion.
